findings.text: The second switch statement's default case (line 167-168) is unreachable because LocalDatetime, LocalDate, and LocalTime are explicitly handled in lines 169-170, but the first switch (lines 158-165) already sets format without a default, so time.Time values with non-local locations will use RFC3339Nano format but then the second switch's default case will never execute the formatting - the logic is inverted and Local* locations will be formatted in UTC instead of preserving their local representation.

The switch on orig.Location() compares against toml.LocalDatetime, toml.LocalDate, and toml.LocalTime which are time.Location pointers, but time.Location comparison by == only works for nil or identical pointers - a time.Time parsed with the same offset but different construction will not match, causing it to fall through to default and be tagged as 'datetime' with timezone instead of the correct local type.
Comment typo: 'Rempve' should be 'Remove' and 'itenm' should be 'items' - while cosmetic, the function comment describes the wrong operation direction.

The localOffset is computed once at package init using time.Now().Zone(), but if the system timezone changes during program execution (rare but possible), all subsequent local datetime parsing will use the stale offset, causing incorrect timezone assignment for datetime-local, date-local, and time-local values.
